SLKN.review: Understand the concepts and expect to write a lot in exams. Classes may feel long, but the grading is good.

AFRN.review: Expect to do substantial self-study, but the instructor gives suggestions before the midterm and final, and questions reportedly come from them.

An understanding, knowledgeable, and supportive instructor who is easy to approach. The quizzes are simple conceptual MCQs, and exam suggestions are provided. Attend regularly and put effort into the assignment. He does not necessarily curve, but makes the course manageable.

MPN.review: Drop this instructor; the reviewer described the grading as average.

ABS3.review: He teaches the material thoroughly using slides, though his speaking pace is slow. Quizzes vary in difficulty; follow both lectures and slides. Suggestions help with written exams, and good writing earns good marks. There is a presentation, and he values class participation. Grading is fair, with no curve or de-curve.

Easygoing and teaches well; exams are fairly easy, and communicating with him helps. However, the reviewer felt grading could be biased and said some students received high grades while others were de-curved.
Avoid him: the reviewer said questions can be difficult and that he may de-curve grades.
The reviewer felt he tends to give around a B on average.

AHB.review: Easygoing and gives good marks on exams; considered a good choice for grading.
Attend class and take notes on his lectures. The slides can be tedious, so study regularly and focus on the topics he marks before exams for a decent grade.

There is no curve and attendance is strict. The first two quizzes have difficult MCQs and carry substantial marks, but he gives generous marks on written work. The reviewer also found the classes boring.
The reviewer had a very positive personal experience and described him as an exceptional faculty member.

He gives suggestions during lectures, so attend regularly. The first two quizzes are MCQ and true/false; aim for full marks. He gives presentations and a group report, marks individual report contributions, and expects you to follow his instructions. Put in consistent effort.

RHU.review: Open and liberal in class, though some political, social, cultural, or religious comments may offend. Participate and visit office hours. Quizzes are easy MCQs; midterms and finals have broad comparison questions connecting current Bangladesh to lecture topics. Use a clear essay structure with relevant examples.

The reviewer found the lectures difficult to sit through and felt that little relevant material was taught. They described the analytical questions as difficult and the solo presentation and viva as stressful.

IZN.review: A kind and easygoing instructor, but the course requires extensive effort and memorization. The syllabus is large, written answers need detail, and the reviewer felt marking was strict with no curve; they advised choosing another faculty if possible.
Described as a pressure-cooker course: earning an A or A- is very difficult, requiring extensive study and precise answers, with little credit for mistakes and a very large syllabus.
